column2: - **FL-8 UPS — the Unicenta POS Strategy: ONE DocAction, at the processor (owner, 2026-10-26: *"UPS is Unicenta POS Strategy. Which we already noted prior that it does not need to handle Docaction locally as there's no need to do any posting. At server those are done to return just replenish movement. Harden the specs to grasp this UPS well as dual Docaction may results on ghost and loss of single source of truth."*).** (a) The point of action (the POS station) only DECLARES: the lines (product, qty, uom) under its ticket key POSStation/Date/Order# (§16.16a). It does NOT complete, post, reserve, or create shipments or invoices — **no DocAction on the station**; its own stock deduction is an advisory copy (FL-2). (b) The PROCESSOR (the HQ/server role) receives the declaration, authors the document, runs the DocAction **once** (Complete + posting), and returns only what the station needs: the **replenishment movement** (product, qty). (c) **Every document has exactly ONE DocAction executor, named by the plan.** No other device runs completeIt / posting for it — not even "deterministically". Reason, measured: a second run mints its own ids (1–3 generated uu per Complete, §36.1 T3(e)), its own document numbers (§36.1 T3(b)) and its own Fact_Acct lines → **GHOST records** (two shipments, two postings for one sale) and **a second source of truth** that can drift. (d) FL-2's 2026-10-25 reword ("in a mesh every member runs the same fold") covers derived VALUES that are recomputed and never stored as records of their own (a stock sum, a balance, a rank). **It never licenses running a DocAction or a posting on more than one device.** (e) The single run's consequences are not broadcast either: each other role receives only the flows the plan declares for it (the station: replenishment). In a peer team (mesh) the executor of a document is its author's device (or the role the plan names); the others receive its declared outputs — they never re-run it. **Planned witness `W-UPS-ONE-DOCACTION` (spec only, not built):** COMPILE — a plan in which two roles could run a DocAction on the same document flow, or a station role is given one, is REFUSED (`dual-docaction` / `station-docaction`); SIMULATOR — a station that completes a declared ticket is caught (its derived rows have no counterpart at the processor = ghost count > 0) and the processor's single run is the only source of M_InOut / Fact_Acct for that ticket; MUTANT — allow a second executor → the ghost arm turns red. **ENFORCED, not just described (owner, 2026-10-26: *"So the Replication Engine enforces that well besides dictating such data flow."*) — today NOTHING enforces FL-8 (the plan is `tables-only`; any device can Complete and its whole consequence group is broadcast); the engine must enforce it in three layers, each witnessed:** **E1 COMPILE** — a document flow row names its ONE executor role (`docaction: {role, actions}`); the compiler refuses a plan with two executor roles for the same document type (`dual-docaction`) or a station/declaring role as executor (`station-docaction`). **E2 LEGACY ACCESS (twin, same L&F)** — the compiled plan is projected onto iDempiere's OWN mechanism, `AD_Document_Action_Access` (per role × document type × action; legacy check `MRole.checkActionAccess`, `MRole.java:2685`; already read by our model layer, `erp/model_master.js:335`): a station role simply has no Complete in its DocAction list, exactly as a legacy role without that access would see it — no new UI rule. **E3 ADMISSION (every device, same verdict)** — the comm fold refuses a DocAction op group whose author's role is not the plan's executor for that document type: `REFUSED not-executor` (same pattern as `not-admin`), so a modified or rogue device cannot introduce a second source of truth — its ghost rows never reach anyone's books, and the refusal is visible. `W-UPS-ONE-DOCACTION` judges E1 (compile refusals), E2 (the projected access rows = the plan, X of N document types) and E3 (a station-authored Complete REFUSED `not-executor` on every device; the processor's Complete MERGED; mutants: E3 check off → the ghost arm red; E1 check off → the dual plan compiles). *(Numbered FL-8 on 2026-10-26: it was first written as "FL-7", which already names deterrence over prevention, §16.17 — the commit messages 043597bea…38f359444 say "FL-7 UPS"; they mean this rule.)*

**⚠ SUPERSEDED 2026-10-26 by FL-8 (UPS):** the paragraph above reads "feasible IF four things are built" as if every peer would derive — WITHDRAWN. Under UPS: only the processor completes and posts; the station declares and receives replenishment. So (1) the from-status guard becomes **processor idempotency** (the same ticket key twice = one document, one Complete; a replayed intent never closes); (2) deterministic generated ids are **not needed** (one executor mints the only ids); (3) a model-version tag matters only for a party that re-runs to AUDIT, not to derive. G9 is now: which flows does each ROLE receive, with one DocAction executor per document.

**§37 / §38 FILM DIRECTION (owner, 2026-10-26: *"Thus your last film/a revolve round these concepts and we are now ironing out execution issues before making a proper mock up demo film that is finishing rather than repeating the previous."*):** the §37 English film is a CONCEPT round; its Chapter 3 ("a second device can work the results out") is superseded by FL-8 — do not reuse that chapter, and do not finish its held Thai cut. The NEXT film is a **finishing demo**, not a repeat: the WORKING UPS flow on real mobile-phone mockups of the apps' own screens — a station declares a sale (lines only, ticket key) → the processor completes + posts ONCE → the replenishment movement arrives back on the station's phone → a station that tries to Complete is refused (`not-executor`, FL-8 E3) — every value on screen from a witness log. It is made only after §38 G-1..G-4 are ✅.
